subject: MSA redlines — reverse indemnity, IP assertion process, and damage cap proposals
messages:
From: Jordan Milton <jm@solarahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Tsu <emily.tsu@solarahealth.com>, Mark Davenport <mdavenport@solarahealth.com>, contracts@harrisonlaw.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Solara redlines — IP infringement & defense allocation (v3)

Team,

Thanks for the MSA — attached are Solara's redlines (v3) with a couple of escalation points for Redwood counsel. Two core asks:

1) Reverse indemnity for third-party IP claims: Solara is asking Redwood to defend and indemnify Solara for third-party claims arising from the services, including model outputs, subject to the usual limitations (no indemnity for Customer modifications).

2) Cap and coverage mechanics: we propose Redwood's exposure be capped at the greater of (a) aggregate fees paid under the Order Form in the prior 12 months, or (b) $5M. Solara is pushing for a higher floor and wants defense control preserved with Customer counsel oversight (i.e., Redwood selects counsel but Solara has approval rights and can participate).

We also included a carveout request for open-source components (they want to exclude obligations for upstream OSS license issues unless Redwood shipped non-compliant binaries).

Please review and propose specific edits. We can escalate to GC if we can't find middle ground — procurement would like to keep timelines short.

Attachments: Solara_MSA_redlines_v3.docx, OrderForm_Solara_20260720.pdf

Regards,
Jordan
Jordan Milton
General Counsel, Solara Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Milton <jm@solarahealth.com>, Emily Tsu <emily.tsu@solarahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, contracts@harrisonlaw.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 13:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Solara redlines — IP infringement & defense allocation (v3)

Jordan / Emily —

Thanks for the detailed pass and the redlines. High level reaction from our side: we understand the ask, but we have three major concerns that prevent us from accepting the reverse indemnity as drafted:

- Breadth: The proposal as written covers "services" and "outputs" broadly; we need to narrow to Third‑Party IP Claims arising from (i) our model weights or (ii) our proprietary connectors. We cannot accept indemnity for customer-prompts or creative outputs where the customer substantially modifies the model or pipelines.

- Defense control / settlement: We can agree to defend, but need the ability to select counsel and control settlement authority subject to a reasonableness/notice clause. Unlimited settlement without Redwood consent is a non-starter.

- Cap: We are open to a cap but prefer a deterministic formula that aligns to the size of the deployment (e.g., 12x monthly committed fees or aggregate fees in 12 months). The $5M floor is higher than we generally accept for customers at this stage.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll circulate a redline response with targeted language limiting scope and clarifying OSS carveouts.
2) Marissa, can you run numbers on the 12x vs aggregate caps and confirm how that impacts the commercials?
3) If we can't settle language via counsel, escalate to Rishi / Lauren for GC-level tradeoffs.

I'll attach our initial response for your comment.

Best,
Olga
VP, Sales (Contracts) | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0182

Attachment: MSA_Redline_Response_OLGA_v1.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Jordan Milton <jm@solarahealth.com>, Emily Tsu <emily.tsu@solarahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Solara redlines — IP infringement & defense allocation (v3)

Olga / Team —

I ran the commercial scenarios and here's a quick summary:

- 12x monthly committed fees (based on their current orderform) yields an effective cap of ~$1.2M — materially below their $5M floor.
- Aggregate fees (prior 12 months) is closer to $900k given onboarding credits; we can offer a multiplier (e.g., 1.5x aggregate) to move closer to their ask without jumping to $5M.
- If we concede defense + indemnity for model-weight-origin claims only, the incremental risk is manageable at a 1.5x aggregate cap.

Recommendation: accept a narrow indemnity for Third‑Party IP Claims where the claim arises solely from Redwood-delivered model weights or Redwood‑provided, unmodified connectors, with a monetary cap = max(1.5x aggregate fees in prior 12 months, $750k). Include an explicit OSS carveout: excludes claims solely based on upstream OSS licensing unless Redwood distributed non-compliant build artifacts.

If counsel is comfortable, I'll propose the above and request confirmation. If Solara pushes back on the cap number, we'll need Rishi to weigh in on whether to stretch to $1.5M.

-Marissa
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Solara redlines — IP infringement & defense allocation (v3)

Thanks for the quick analysis, Marissa. A few clarifying points from Solara's perspective:

- The reason we asked for a $5M floor is that our deployment is expected to scale quickly; the risk exposure from IP claims (defense + damages) can exceed immediate revenue in a worst-case event.
- Solara is open to the "model‑weights only" limitation as long as the definition is clear and includes "services as delivered by Redwood" (i.e., preconfigured models and connectors).
- Regarding defense, we prefer to preserve meaningful oversight (approval of counsel, right to decline settlement that would impose ongoing obligations). Full unilateral settlement by Redwood would require an exception.

If you can send a redline with the proposed language today we can take an internal read and respond. Procurement (Mark) is pushing to get this signed before the end of the month.

—Emily
Senior Counsel, Solara Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Tsu <emily.tsu@solarahealth.com>, Jordan Milton <jm@solarahealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Mark Davenport <mdavenport@solarahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Final language proposal — Third‑party IP indemnity (agreement in principle)

Team,

After internal review, Redwood is prepared to accept the following compromise language (redline attached) to resolve the Solara MSA IP indemnity escalation:

- Scope: Redwood will indemnify and defend Customer for Third‑Party IP Claims to the extent such claims arise solely from (i) Redwood‑provided model weights and (ii) Redwood‑supplied, unmodified connectors and adapters packaged as part of the Service.
- OSS carveout: claims that are based solely on upstream open‑source license compliance are excluded unless Redwood distributed a non‑compliant build artifact or explicitly represented compatibility.
- Defense and settlement: Redwood will have primary control of defense. Customer may reasonably approve selected lead counsel; if Customer withholds approval, parties will meet to resolve. Redwood must obtain Customer consent for any settlement that imposes ongoing obligations or non‑monetary injunctive relief.
- Cap: Monetary liability for indemnifiable Third‑Party IP Claims will be capped at the greater of (a) 1.5x aggregate fees paid under the Order Form in the preceding 12 months, or (b) $750,000.

We believe this narrows the exposure while giving Solara meaningful protections. If Solara accepts in principle, we can circulate a final redline for signature and DocuSign.

Attachments: MSA_Redline_Response_OLGA_v1.docx

Please confirm and we'll trigger the DocuSign flow.

-Rishi
